1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6.name: Sicilian Defence: Modern Variations
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6.background: Black's most common move after 2.Nf3. It is the gateway to the Najdorf, Dragon, Scheveningen and Classical Variations, which arise after 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4.strategy: Challenges the c5-pawn at once and opens the game. After ...cxd4 White recaptures with a knight, trading a central pawn for a flank pawn in return for quick development and open lines for both bishops. Black gets a central pawn majority and the c-file.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4.name: Sicilian Defence

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.Bb5+.strategy: Develops with check and prepares castling, a way to sidestep the heavy theory of the open game. White can aim for a clamp on d5 with pawns on c4 and e4 after exchanging the bishop, or for a broad pawn centre built calmly. A sound, low-risk choice.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.Bb5+.name: Sicilian Defence: Moscow Variation
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.Bb5+.background: Also called the Canal–Sokolsky Attack, after Esteban Canal and Alexey Sokolsky, who began playing it in the 1940s. Sokolsky played it twice at the 1947 Chigorin Memorial. Kasparov played it in his game Kasparov versus the World.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.c3.strategy: Prepares a broad pawn centre and takes the c3 square from the b1-knight, which can then no longer help guard e4. That makes e4 a target for Black's development, so White has to look after it before the centre is built. Solid, but slower than the open game.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.c3.name: Sicilian Defence: Delayed Alapin Variation, with d6

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.Bd3.strategy: Guards e4 and prepares castling, but the bishop stands directly in front of the d-pawn, which cannot advance until the bishop moves. White gives up the sharp open game for a slower build-up, and Black can develop freely.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.Bd3.name: Sicilian Defence: Kopec System

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.g3.strategy: Prepares a fianchetto: the bishop on g2 will back up e4 and watch the long diagonal. White avoids the sharp open game for slower manoeuvring play, which gives Black time to develop and take space in the centre.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.b4.strategy: Offers a pawn to pull Black's c-pawn away from d4, so that White can occupy the centre. White gets space and quick development, but is a pawn down, and once Black has taken, the pawn on b4 is an annoyance that eyes c3, where the b1-knight wants to go.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.b4.name: Sicilian Defence: Wing Gambit, Deferred Variation

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.Bb5+ Bd7.strategy: The main way out of the check: the bishop invites an exchange of light-squared bishops and leaves the b8-knight free for c6. Black gets a solid, compact position and accepts that White keeps the choice of how to use the centre.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.Bb5+ Nc6.strategy: Blocks with the natural developing move, but the knight is pinned and cannot yet influence the centre, so Black plans to unpin with the c8-bishop. White can try to trade bishop for knight and double Black's pawns, or keep the tension and castle.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.c3 Nf6.strategy: Develops with tempo against e4, which the pawn on c3 has left without help from the b1-knight. White must find another defender before the centre can be built, and Black gets an active, comfortable game.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4.strategy: Takes the pawn and trades a flank pawn for White's central one. Black gets the semi-open c-file and two central pawns against one, while White recaptures and gains a lead in development.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 Nf6.strategy: Attacks e4 before any exchange, so White has to defend it, and the knight on c3 that does so takes away the c-pawn's push for a clamp on d5. The price is that White gains an extra option of taking on c5, which leads to unclear, double-edged play.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.g3 b5.strategy: Hangs a pawn for nothing: 4.Bxb5+ wins it with check, since nothing guards b5, and Black has no lead in development to make up for it. White needs only to finish developing, and the quiet g3 set-up is not slow enough to justify a sacrifice.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.g3 b5.name: Sicilian Defence: Kotov Gambit
